capabilities.target: Identity provider user directory profile and group memberships
Identity provider MFA factors and temporary access pass issuance
Chat delivery of temporary access pass to ticket requester

inputs.source: Support tickets, including tickets emailed in by contractors and vendors

instructions.note: The prompt instructs the agent to reset MFA and send the temporary pass to the ticket opener, treating ticket content and requester identity as sufficient authority.
The design relies on an approval instruction in the prompt for the sensitive reset action, with no declared structural recipient confirmation for the temporary pass destination.

controls.name: Service desk analyst approval in the queue tool
controls.decay_rationale: The approval is enforced outside the model, but effectiveness decays with analyst volume and is defeated if autonomy is increased or the gate is removed.

controls.name: Recipient confirmation bound to account owner record for temporary pass delivery

findings.title: Confused deputy / credential reset fraud: untrusted ticket can trigger MFA reset for a target account and send the temporary pass to the ticket opener

attack_path.note: Contractors and vendors can email tickets in; requester is the email sender.
Agent looks up the user profile and memberships.
Agent resets MFA after analyst approval.
Temporary pass is sent to whoever opened the ticket.

findings.residual_rationale: The wired approval gate only covers cap.mfa_reset, not the identity binding between the reset target and the recipient of cap.send_temp_pass. High-volume raw approval narrows one step, but the design still lacks any structural recipient confirmation, so the irreversible restricted secret can still be delivered to the ticket opener after an approved reset.

forecast.watch_signal: Approval gate removed or narrowed, autonomy raised, or sustained analyst queue volume remains about 400 approvals per shift across two analysts.

evidence.observation: The prompt directs the agent to look up the user, reset MFA, and send the temporary access pass to the person who opened the ticket.
Analysts see the exact reset target, requester, and full ticket body before approving the reset action.
The queue shows the exact target account, the requester, and the full ticket text, so the gate is raw action review.
Two analysts approve about 400 requests per shift and most are routine, indicating high approval volume and approval fatigue risk.
Contractors and vendors can email tickets in, and the requester field is the email sender, so an outside party can author the initiating content.
The temporary pass goes to whoever opened the ticket, not to the account owner, leaving no structural binding between reset target and secret recipient.

recommendations.action: Bind temporary pass delivery to the account owner record or a preverified channel, not to the ticket opener or email sender.
Require analyst verification that the requester is authorized for the target account, or require a second factor from the account owner before MFA reset issuance completes.
Reduce approval fatigue by lowering per-analyst approval volume or adding risk-based escalation for requester-target mismatches and contractor-originated tickets.

findings.title: Property finding: analyst approval queue is vulnerable to consent fatigue at declared volume
findings.residual_rationale: Rubric step 2 would normally lower this property finding to moderate because a raw-action approval gate is present, but the same design fact being assessed is that the gate operates at about 400 routine approvals per shift across two analysts. That declared volume materially undermines the gate's real effectiveness beyond what the classification fields can express for this property finding, so residual is kept at high.

forecast.watch_signal: Per-analyst approvals remain well above about 20 per day, approvals are remembered or streamlined, or the queue workload rises further.

evidence.observation: Two analysts approve about 400 requests per shift and most are routine, which meets the rubric's high-volume condition and weakens the gate.
The queue presents repetitive approve or reject decisions on reset requests, making fatigue materially relevant to the effectiveness of the gate.

recommendations.action: Add automated mismatch detection and escalation so analysts only review high-risk reset requests instead of the full routine stream.

stride_coverage.rationale: No capability to modify prompt, tools, memory, or agent configuration is declared in the reviewed design.
No spend, looping execution, recursive delegation, or long-running autonomous task capability is described in the artifacts.
The inbound ticket flow introduces data into the system, but the reviewed artifacts do not show secret disclosure on that ingress edge itself.
The design does not describe queue flooding, rate exhaustion, or runtime limits tied to this inbound flow.
This outbound flow is reviewed as a delivery edge; the key risk here is recipient disclosure, not in-transit alteration described by the artifacts.
No availability degradation or transport exhaustion controls or issues are described for the outbound temporary pass flow.
The artifacts do not state whether approval queue records are tamper-evident or protected from unauthorized modification.
The artifacts do not say who can read queue records or whether ticket bodies in the queue expose confidential information beyond intended reviewers.

rating.rationale: The highest present risk is a critical untrusted-ticket path to identity reconfiguration and irreversible delivery of a temporary access pass to the ticket opener. The declared analyst approval gate is a structural raw-action review, but its stated volume is high and it does not bind the reset target to the recipient of the temporary pass. Manual validation only; no scripts were run.

limitations: This assessment reflects the declared design and configuration artifacts provided here, not observed runtime behavior or tested enforcement in production.
No source code, IdP policy configuration, recipient binding logic, chat channel trust model, or ticket authentication controls were provided; confidence is therefore limited to the declared workflow.
No explicit audit logging, queue integrity controls, or sender verification mechanisms were described, so those properties could only be marked not_assessed or inferred from the narrative.
